text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure, reduce stroke risk, and protect the kidneys in people with type 2 diabetes. While generally well-tolerated, it can cause several side effects.
Most common side effects are mild and often improve over time as your body adjusts:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly, known as orthostatic hypotension)
Upper respiratory symptoms like a stuffy or runny nose, sneezing, or cold-like discomfort
Digestive issues such as mild nausea, diarrhea, or stomach upset

text_blocks.snippet: Seek medical attention right away if you experience any of these rare but dangerous reactions:

list.snippet: Severe allergic reactions (Anaphylaxis): Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing or swallowing.
High potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, numbness or tingling, or a slow, fast, or irregular heartbeat.
Kidney problems: Little to no urination, swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet, or unexplained weight gain.
Very low blood pressure: Extreme dizziness, fainting, or severe lightheadedness.
Liver issues: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or severe upper stomach pain.

text_blocks.snippet: More detailed safety and dosing data can be reviewed on the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide and GoodRx Losartan Side Effects Overview.
